notes: ACCESS: no WAF/Imperva block encountered -- direct fetch worked throughout (unlike the David Jones Home sibling S.N. 209 on the same 'Australian department store' flag, which needed a translate.goog proxy for an Incapsula interstitial). robots.txt checked first (Rule 3): standard facet/sort/search/account/login disallows plus a few promo-department blocks (women/men/beauty/kidsbaby/electrical/gifts/offers) -- none cover the Home department or apply to this extraction, no Claude-specific disallow present. PLATFORM: myer.com.au runs on IBM WebSphere-Commerce-style URLs (/webapp/wcs/... disallowed in robots.txt) with a Next.js storefront on top, and Fredhopper (Attraqt) as the search/merchandising/category-listing engine. Every category page embeds a Next.js '__NEXT_DATA__' script tag containing a React-Query dehydratedState with a queryKey ['category', <path>, ...] whose data payload has an exact 'productTotalCount' integer field (alongside the full first-page productList/skus) -- this was used as the qty source throughout. COUNT VERIFICATION (Rule 1): exhaustion-checked on 6 categories spanning small and large, across departments -- Mirrors (213: page5/offset192 returns 21 items reaching exactly 213, page6 returns 0), Decorative Accessories (860: last page offset816 returns 44 reaching 860, next page 0), Wall Art (807), Coffee Mugs (492: last page offset480 returns 12 reaching 492, next page 0), Bowls (590), Beer Glasses (7) -- all showed offset+pageLen==productTotalCount exactly and 0 items one page past the boundary with productTotalCount unchanged; additionally did a full unique-SKU crawl across all pages of Dinner Sets (165) confirming 165 distinct product IDs with zero duplicates/inflation. This confirms productTotalCount is a genuine exhaustive total on this Fredhopper platform, not an inflated raw-index count, and was trusted uniformly for the remaining leaves. URL PATTERN: /c/<top-seoToken>/<child-seoToken>/.../<leaf-seoToken>, reconstructed from the site's own global nav tree (a large embedded JSON with categoryId/seoToken/childCategories fields present in every page's HTML, not guessed) and confirmed working. STRUCTURE: site organizes Home under a single 'Home' mega-nav with type-based branches (Home Decor: Photo Frames & Albums / Candles & Home Fragrance / Artificial Plants & Flowers / Vases Pots & Plant Stands / Cushions & Throws / Wall Art Mirrors & Clocks / Lighting / Rugs / Decorative Accessories) plus separate Dining, Bathroom, Kitchen, Bedroom, Furniture, Outdoor, and appliance/books/food departments -- no dual type+room tree found for lighting or decor (no Rule 0.6 duplicate-tree case), the only overlap found was the exact-same categoryIds for 'Pots' (1051151) and 'Plant Stands' (1332587) appearing under both Home Decor>Vases,Pots&PlantStands and Outdoor>Garden -- same listing under two nav paths, evaluated once (see exclusion below), not double-counted. SCOPE/RULE 0 GAINS: traversed the full Lighting branch with no depth limit (Lamps&LampShades / Indoor Lighting / Outdoor Lighting, 10 leaf fixture types) including 'Party Lights' (71) despite the room/occasion-flavoured name -- title-inspected and confirmed genuine festoon/string/rope/fairy lighting fixtures per Rule 0.1/0.2, kept; all mirrors captured across both the Home Decor Wall Art/Mirrors/Clocks node (213) and a separate, distinctly-ID'd Bathroom Mirrors node (47) per Rule 0.3. EXCLUDED with reasons: Candles & Home Fragrance (entire branch -- scented candles/room sprays/oils/diffusers, explicit Home Fragrance exclusion; its 'Lanterns' sub-node was title-checked and found dominated by scented candle SKUs, not decorative lanterns, dropped as a mixed roll-up per Rule 0/'drop don't pad'); Artificial Plants & Flowers (explicit exclude); Cushions & Throws (textile, shares categoryId with the Bedroom department's identical node); Rugs (floor textile); 'Pots' sub-node of Vases,Pots&PlantStands (33 items, title-checked -- dominated by functional garden/self-watering pots, vertical-garden panels and raised-garden-bed kits, i.e. gardening equipment not decorative planters, dropped as a mixed roll-up; same categoryId duplicated under Outdoor>Garden, so nothing lost); 'Plant Stands' sub-node (35 items, title-checked -- metal tiered shelf/rack stands, functional plant-display furniture, dropped; same categoryId duplicated under Outdoor>Garden). Dining: Cutlery and Barware (explicit cutlery/bar-tools exclude, Barware title-spot-checked as shaker/ice-bucket-led consistent with the Rule 3 David Jones precedent); Table Linen & Accessories' Napkins/Placemats/Table Runners/Tablecloths (textile) -- but its sibling 'Coasters' sub-node (75) was title-checked and found genuinely wood/cork/ceramic decorative coasters, kept. Bathroom: Bath Towels/Bath Mats/Bathrobes (textile), Bathroom Accessories' Organisation/Toilet Brushes/Soap Dispensers/Scales (functional/hygiene, same pattern as the David Jones Bathroom Accessories precedent) and Cleaning -- only Bathroom Mirrors kept from that department. Entire Kitchen department (Cookware/Knives/Utensils/Baking/Tea&CoffeeMaking-equipment/Lunch&Drink/KitchenLinen), Kitchen/Household/Personal-Care Appliances, Bedroom (textile/furniture), Furniture (all), Outdoor (Beach&Pool/Picnicware/BBQ/OutdoorTech/Camping/VehicleAccessories -- no decorative items beyond the already-evaluated duplicate Garden pots/stands), Food&Hampers, Books&Stationery: skipped, purely functional/excluded product types, no decorative subcategory found. 'Top Brands', 'Now Trending', 'New', 'All Home': skipped per NEVER EXTRACT (brand-listing/trending/new-arrivals/shop-all pages). TABLEWARE SCOPE NOTE: 'Cups & Mugs' (Cups & Saucers/Coffee Mugs/Espresso Cups) included under Kitchen & Dining alongside Dinnerware/Serveware/Glassware, treated as part of the tableware/dinnerware family the same way the brief explicitly includes Glassware 'all -- decorative and functional'; this is a judgment call flagged here for merge-time review since the brief's INCLUDE list does not name mugs/cups specifically. No duplicate-company flag applies to S.N. 217 in the brief (S.N. 209 David Jones Home is flagged only as a same-genre sibling for access-route reference, not a same-domain duplicate).
